counterevidence_considered.description: The only repetition present anywhere in the table is of treatment labels (each of 'rewetted' and 'drained' appears on five rows). This is ordinary group structure rather than repeated entry of an independent unit, since every basin_id is distinct, so it does not support the issue class.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: treatment labels repeat 5x each; basin_id values are all distinct

evidence.description: The data description states one row is one basin measured once, names basin_id as the independent unit, and asserts every code appears on exactly one row with no repeated sampling.
evidence.observed_value: 10 rows for 10 basins; every basin_id on exactly one row

source_refs.quoted_text: so the table holds ten rows for ten basins with no repeated sampling.
- basin_id: the survey code of the basin; every code appears on exactly one row.

One row is: one peat basin, measured once at the end of the growing season
Independent unit column: basin_id

evidence.description: The input CSV contains exactly ten data rows with ten distinct basin_id values (PB-01 through PB-10); no independent unit occupies more than one row.
The workflow enforces one row per basin, raising an error if any basin code is duplicated before analysis runs.
The permutation procedure enumerates combinations of the ten row indices, so each basin contributes exactly one value to every split; the randomisation unit and the analysis unit coincide.
evidence.observed_value: combinations over 10 row indices, choose 5; C(10,5)=252

evidence.description: The report's stated numbers are internally consistent and reproduce by hand: rewetted mean (21.5+17.6+28.3+23.2+26.1)/5 = 23.34, drained mean (15.2+12.3+24.7+14.1+18.4)/5 = 16.94, contrast +6.40 mg/L, 252 = C(10,5) splits, 16/252 = 0.0635, and the non-significance conclusion follows from those numbers.

source_refs.quoted_text:
Observed contrast (rewetted minus drained): +6.40 mg/L.
Splits at least as extreme as the observed one: 16 of 252.

[selected-result] Exact two-sided permutation test over 252 basin-to-treatment splits: mean DOC is +6.40 mg/L higher in rewetted basins (23.34 vs 16.94 mg/L), p = 0.0635 (16/252 splits at least as extreme), which does not reach the 0.05 level.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by searching for any way an independent unit enters the procedure more than once: (1) scanned all ten CSV rows for duplicate basin_id values (none; PB-01..PB-10 are distinct); (2) checked whether the workflow re-reads, joins, or expands rows before testing (it does not; it reads the CSV once and errors on duplicate codes); (3) checked whether the permutation loop could reuse a row within a split (combinations over row indices cannot repeat an index); (4) recomputed the group means, contrast, split count C(10,5)=252, and p = 16/252 = 0.0635 by hand, which match the report exactly. The one thing I could not independently reproduce without code execution (Bash was disabled) is the tail count of 16 extreme splits, but that count is orthogonal to the issue class, and the enumeration logic producing it is correct. No route to the claimed issue class survived.
